R182.note: RFC 4515 filter-value escaping applied before concatenation into the LDAP filter; correct sink shape, no observable behavior change for legitimate values.

R183.note: escapeshellarg() applied to both fallback exec arguments; matches stated contract (return/discard semantics unchanged).

R184.note: Replaces Runtime.exec with Files.list(Paths.get(data)); eliminates the shell entirely while preserving the directory-listing-by-data behavior.

R185.note: Raw-socket FTP command building replaced with Apache Commons Net FTPClient.retrieveFile(), a structured API rather than string concatenation; the incidental fix of the literal-string password bug is disclosed in the explanation and only helps legitimate use.

R186.note: StackExchange.Redis/RESP framing correctly closes the delimiter-injection vector, but the constructor's dependency type changes from TcpClient to IConnectionMultiplexer, a breaking API change for any existing composition-root caller (disclosed in the write-up but not shown fixed elsewhere).

R187.note: escapeshellarg() applied to $host in the system() call; minimal, correct, no other behavior change.

R188.note: Quoting escapes only backslash and double-quote; IMAP is line-oriented so an embedded CRLF in the folder name still terminates the command early and injects a new one regardless of the surrounding quotes, leaving the primary command-injection vector open.

R189.note: Same correct RFC 4515 filter escaping as R182, applied at the right point before filter construction.

R190.note: Containment check via Clean+Abs+separator-bounded prefix correctly blocks real traversal, but the earlier raw strings.HasPrefix(name, "..") pre-filter also rejects legitimate filenames that merely start with two literal dots (e.g. "..config"), an undisclosed added restriction not required by the fix.

R191.note: Allowlist mapping command verbs to fixed handler names is the correct primary defense for arbitrary call_user_func_array dispatch; restricting to known commands is the intended fix shape for this CWE, not an incidental over-restriction.

R192.note: path.relative(base,target).startsWith('..') check correctly blocks real escapes but also false-positives on legitimate filenames that literally start with ".." directly under the base directory, since it lacks a separator/equality boundary check.

R193.note: Build FAILS (missing import java.io.File, 'cannot find symbol'); the fix as delivered does not compile, so it silently cannot ship, which the write-up does not flag.

R194.note: realpath()-based containment check plus rejection of ':' '/' '\\' correctly closes both the stream-wrapper bypass and traversal; the flat-filename restriction matches the case's own stated design intent (chdir into a single reports directory), not an arbitrary new limitation.

R195.note: Identical fix and identical bug to R190: correct separator-bounded containment check, but the earlier raw ".." prefix rejection on the unresolved input still false-positives on legitimate filenames starting with two literal dots.
